gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada has a high, squared-off x-height and terminals that stop well short of the stem. And Blockletter, drawn with a pressure-free ballpoint line, does its best work large, where the body font is better at running text.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-latin: Precise in the heading, neutral in the text: Blockletter draws every stroke at one thickness, while Anek Latin keeps its lowercase tall and its curves held open. One makes a statement, the other just carries the words.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-malayalam: Clean, contemporary letters carry the text here, with curve tips that never touch. Blockletter lays its line out like spaghetti and shines at display size, while Anek Malayalam is the one built for steady reading in a plain sans voice.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-odia: Anek Odia keeps its rounds unsealed, like an unlatched hook. Make Blockletter small and its tall, pen-less strokes lose their punch, and enlarge the plain sans body and its capitals, only slightly above lowercase, feel timid.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-tamil: Blockletter outlines its counters in a single steady line, precise and modern. Anek Tamil is the softer partner, with big round lowercase bowls and half-unwrapped c and s shapes that make a paragraph feel easy.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anek-telugu: Blockletter has a thickness like neon glass tubing, which makes it a showpiece for big, short lines. Anek Telugu takes over below it, a clean, approachable sans-serif whose wide, tall bowls set the reading rhythm.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-anuphan: Blockletter looks like neon tubing bent into letters, constant in thickness and precise. But Anuphan is the quiet one, with big round lowercase bowls and open curves that leave clear gaps.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-arimo: Blockletter has no hairlines and no swells, just a tall belly and a pencil that never presses harder. Arimo takes the quieter job, a sans-serif with a tall mean line and spacious gaps in its rounded glyphs.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-armata: Precise from the first word, Blockletter draws stems and crossbars at one thickness and earns its keep big and short. Armata follows with generous spacing, open terminals and lowercase bodies that fill most of the letter height.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-athiti: A pencil-sketched line that never presses harder gives Blockletter its tall, squat-bellied display character, like sign-shop vinyl cut to one width. Athiti, a sans with a high mean line and open s shapes, gives it room.
